description: Stable Ensembl IDs join drug targets to disease-linked proteins. Direct target overlap, STRING physical-network RWR and shared lowest-level Reactome pathway membership provide distinct kinds of association. They do not establish whether inhibiting or activating a target will help; the jury assesses that direction from the supplied evidence.
Open Targets · ChEMBL · STRING 12.5 · Reactome · regulatory sources · RCSB PDB
Random Walk with Restart on the physical protein network contributes 10 places; direct disease–target evidence contributes 5. Overlaps are removed and places refilled where coverage allows.
GPT-5.4 (openai-gpt-5.4), GLM-5.3 (glm-5.3) and Kimi K3 (kimi-k3) through Snowflake Cortex. GLM and Kimi use low reasoning effort; the current prompt is jury-v7.

All three models examine the same source-grounded evidence. Candidate order is independently shuffled and network rankings are withheld. JSON schema, citation IDs, numeric claims and ranks are checked. Borda consensus requires at least two valid jurors; Kendall’s W and disagreements remain inspectable.

Evidence items retain E-ID, statement, numeric values, source ID, URL and release. Mechanism descriptions are embedded unchanged; association, bioactivity and pathway statements are constructed from structured records. Jurors see the candidate-bound IDs, statements and values, and must cite supporting or contradictory items. Stored rationales and objections retain the model’s exact wording.

Experiments and settings, candidate evidence JSONB, jurors, jury votes and docking metadata persist in PostgreSQL. The API reconstructs the blinded packet from saved candidate evidence. File references and checksums point to large graph and pose files held in file storage. Saved experiments can be reopened, compared, archived and restored.

Docker-based preparation with RDKit and Meeko prepares molecular inputs for AutoDock Vina. Supported drug–protein pairs use experimental RCSB PDB structures. Predicted binding poses can be inspected in 3D; docking does not determine candidate ranking.
Protein paths explain shortest-path proximity, rather than RWR diffusion. Rankings, AI reviews and docking poses remain hypotheses for investigation.
